title: JP-8SweepPad — estimated opening excerpt
method: Source-only analysis: mono 22050 Hz decoding of the original Roland MP3, 8192-sample Hann STFT at 256-sample hops, nonnegative least-squares decomposition against detune-broadened harmonic templates over MIDI 36–88, and inspection of local FFT peaks and amplitude transitions. Candidate notes were screened for upper-harmonic and subharmonic errors. The first sustained chord has clear independent low families near 87/131/196 Hz (F2/C3/G3). At about 4.1 seconds it shifts up three semitones to roughly 104/156/233 Hz (Ab2/Eb3/Bb3). A slow descending concentration of spectral energy and gradual amplitude swell distinguish the pad from the other examples. Octave-related peaks are not automatically added as additional keys.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. Every event here is estimated from the MP3, not an exact original MIDI event.
Velocity 100 is an explicit placeholder. Original velocities, sustain pedal, pitch bend, modulation and other controller events are unavailable and are not recovered.

Sounding pitch families do not uniquely determine played keys when oscillator octave offsets or layered tones are unknown. This transcription uses sounding fundamentals with a newly designed patch at zero overall transpose.
MP3 encoding, detuned oscillators, effects and envelope release obscure key-down and key-up times. The MIDI contains practical gates, not measured hardware key releases.
The patch is newly authored in Septum from spectral and temporal cues. It is an approximation of the named factory sound, not Roland factory SysEx or a recovered hardware preset.
Long filter and amplifier attacks hide exact initial key-down timing; the two chord starts and releases are uncertain by roughly 150–300 ms.
The true voicing may contain octave-doubled notes or layered transposed oscillators; three independent sounding fundamentals per chord are used here.
The 8.15-second boundary excludes the third chord’s onset and ends during the second chord’s release.

patch_design.name: APX JP8 Pad
rationale: Broadly detuned saw-like ridges and a slow amplitude swell suggest a layered saw pad with long attack and release.
A negative filter envelope is an authored hypothesis for the descending bright-to-dark sweep visible at each chord onset.
Moderate resonance emphasizes the moving spectral band; quiet chorus-like delay and a longer reverb approximate the diffuse tail.

The first render removed nearly all upper harmonics after the sweep, whereas the recording retains a diffuse bright band. A 12 dB low-pass, modestly higher base cutoff and shallower/slower negative envelope retain more upper energy; two moderately spread Super Saws and a slower amplifier swell approximate the diffuse source.
uncertainties: No authenticated factory PRESET dump is available; every changed control value is an authored approximation.
The recording does not uniquely reveal oscillator topology, layer routing, filter slope, modulation or effect settings.
Filter polarity and depth are not recovered control values; the slow spectral movement could also result from another envelope or modulation topology.
A first software render informed these control adjustments. This is a conditional audio match using estimated notes, not recovered factory settings or a hardware-calibrated DSP claim.
